claim: Averaging runs of one LLM pipeline gains a small amount of Brier: about 0.003 (Halawi, 6 runs), about 0.004 (AIA, 10 runs vs single, 1,610 questions), about 0.004 (CHAIN, 5 samples), about 0.005 (FutureSearch, 4 mixed-model runs). Mean, median and trimmed mean are equal. LLM re-reading of the runs (universal self-consistency, non-agentic supervisor) is worse than the mean. Most gain arrives by 5 runs. No study holds total tokens equal.
agent_test: At equal tokens compare 1 run x 6 tokens of reasoning vs 6 runs averaged; try trimmed mean vs median.

claim: Run-to-run noise of a single forecast is large; averaging 5 runs cuts SD by about two thirds in one study, and a frontier reasoning model still shows cross-trial SD of about 0.09-0.10 on market questions (BLF, no belief state). About 60% of variance sits in the final judgment step.
agent_test: Measure SD over 20 repeats on 18 questions with fixed vs variable evidence; average 5.

claim: Different models help more than copies, but only if their forecasts are decorrelated: LLM crowd of 12 models matches the human crowd (Brier .20 vs .19); at a fixed 5-sample budget the best team is 4 different models and never all on the best one (Grok 4 least replaceable); gains flatten at about 3 distinct members; seven models with 0.94 mean correlation gave only 0.0047 Brier gain, not significant.
agent_test: Mix 2-3 prompt personas or models vs same prompt x N at equal calls.

claim: Raw averaging gains are small and can be negative for weak base models: Hsieh et al. found GPT-4o base ensembles were worse than a single run (.218 vs .210), while an agentic ReAct ensemble helped slightly (.169-.170 vs .180 single).
agent_test: Test whether averaging helps only when per-run SD is large and the scaffold is calibrated.

claim: Retrieval helps a plain base model (Halawi .206 to .186) and small open models even with leak-free retrieval (Hindcast: 8 of 9 models better, up to 23%), but little once a fine-tuned reasoner is used (.183 to .181), and agentic search with a good provider adds only about 0.009 Brier overall for a strong agent (AIA). Weak search equals no search. It reverses on hype-heavy topics.
agent_test: Ablate retrieval with and without a strong reasoning scaffold at equal tokens.

claim: Retrieval can make forecasts worse: more news pushes the mean forecast up (0.20 with no documents to 0.46 with 3-5); Qwen2.5-7B Brier .159 no retrieval to .250 with RAG. A base-rate prompt cut this to .184 and one forecast per document with a median to .222; neither beat the base-rate-only .127. Hype topics (Billboard #1 questions) hurt retrieval agents.
agent_test: Check forecast shift when adding documents; compare with a constant base rate.

claim: Retrieved evidence is an attack surface: one fabricated article flips 56% of forecasts, 5 flip 69-73%, 10 flip 89%; publisher label is ignored. Allow-lists (spoofed publisher 77% flips), median-over-documents (40-52% at k=5) and perplexity filters (67% still flip at T=1.2) each have a cheap bypass. Leak filters cost about 30% of genuine results (BLF) with 1.5% residual leaks; no tested filter separates poison from real news.
agent_test: Plant a fake article on a test set and measure flips under source-weighting rules.

claim: Date-filtered search leaks future information: leak pages for 71-81% of questions, Brier .108 leaky vs .242 leak-free. Leak-free replays (Hindcast, BLF 4-layer defense with 1.5% residual) still show retrieval gains, so the benefit is real but smaller (about 0.009 Brier for a strong agent, AIA). Halawi's gain with leak-checked retrieval has not been measured.
agent_test: Use only post-cutoff questions or leak-checked retrieval when testing S3.

claim: Retrieval-plus-ensemble LLM forecasters are near but not at crowd level: Halawi .179 vs crowd .149; ForecastBench best LLM about .128 vs superforecasters .096; gap about .017 by Jan 2026 per FRI; Metaculus pros beat bots by 17-20 points in 2024-25 but gap not significant in spring 2026.
agent_test: Track Brier gap to a crowd baseline on a post-cutoff set.

claim: Combining LLM with crowd gives small, selective gains: Halawi weighted system+crowd .149 to .146; AIA price access .116 to .103 without search and .085 to .075 with search (about 0.010-0.013); but the price alone scores .096 and the best prior LLM given the price did worse than the price.
agent_test: Use market price as anchor only for mid-range prices; test shrink toward crowd.

claim: Cassi's crowd adjustment gave nearly 0.01 Brier over its own un-adjusted ensemble per FRI (blog only). Paired against the plain market price, Cassi's market gain is only +0.6 Brier Index points (not significant) and its overall gain over the crowd+prior baseline +1.0 (not significant). The crowd signal itself is worth about 0.010-0.013 in AIA's ablation. So the gain is real as a use of the price, not as a separate novel step; no rule detail is published.
agent_test: Add price-divergence review step and compare with plain ensemble on market questions.

claim: Human-AI interaction: exposing LLMs to the human median improves them (GPT-4 .17 to .14; Claude 2 .22 to .15) but a simple 50/50 average of machine and human beats the updated forecast; LLM assistants raised human accuracy 24-28%.
agent_test: Test simple average with an anchor vs letting the model update toward it.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Many-call ensembles and search are common among winners: 86% of Fall 2025 winners ensemble; winners used about 28 calls vs 7; pro-vs-bot gap shrinks with team size up to about 10 bots; removing search degraded Brier 3.6x in one live eval. xAI Grok 4.20's 8-run average is not separated from its search tools; the only decomposition shows Grok 4 gives ensembles value through decorrelation.
agent_test: Vary call count 1,5,10 and with/without search at equal token budget; note winner stats are observational.

claim: Consistency checks correlate with Brier across forecaster models (Cond r .92/.87 and .71/.69; Negation .60 on one set but -.36 on the other; Or negative on NewsAPI). Part of this is general model strength. A forecaster patched to be consistent did not improve accuracy. No study has used consistency to select or weight ensemble members.
agent_test: Use consistency violation between paired questions as a check on ensemble members.

claim: LLMs over-predict Yes and are underconfident near 0/1; ensembling does not fix this bias: mean forecast 57% when 14 of 31 resolved Yes; RMS calibration .42 vs crowd .38.
agent_test: Check bias of mean forecast against base rate before and after averaging.

claim: Outcome-trained models plus a 7-run ensemble reach .190 vs o1 .202 on Polymarket, still .039 worse than the market; ensembling gives a modest lift on top of training.
agent_test: Not testable without training; ignore for schema.

claim: At equal number of calls, structure beats repeats for a weak model: five independent direct forecasts averaged gained 0.004 Brier while a structured 5-call method gained 0.036 (DeepSeek-V3, 8 datasets). Not equal tokens (structure used 4.9x), and not a search-forecasting setting.
agent_test: Equal-token test: 1 deep run vs k shallow runs averaged vs k runs with different decomposition prompts.

claim: The ensemble gain is mostly a function of how decorrelated the members are: frontier models correlate highly (0.94 in soccer); at fixed budget the optimal team mixes models; pools of different weaker models flatten at about 3 members.
agent_test: Measure pairwise correlation of persona or prompt variants; drop members above 0.9 correlation.

claim: Retrieval inflation has measured fixes: a base-rate-first system prompt (.250 to .184), one forecast per document with a median (.250 to .222), and ensemble then log-odds extremization for the opposite problem of hedging (.1140 to .1076-.1085). None has been tested together on a frontier agent.
agent_test: Start from reference-class prior, move only on evidence type, cap per-document shift, then average and extremize.

claim: LLM re-reading of ensemble members is a trap unless it adds new search: non-agentic supervisor .1168 vs mean .1140 vs agentic supervisor .1125 (AIA); BLF also found the AIA aggregator worse than the mean.
agent_test: Compare mean vs LLM-judge aggregation; give the judge a search step and a confidence-gated override.

claim: Top ForecastBench agents are within 1-3 Brier Index points of each other and of the plain market price on market questions once paired; most differences are not significant.
agent_test: Always evaluate with paired comparisons against a price+base-rate baseline.
